comment: T-078's table: one row for each of the 72 decisions bootstrap0/src/gen.c,
gen_expr.c, gen_stmt.c and gen_data.c cite, and four second-facet probes whose
decision ends in a letter. T-154 adds 12 output-branch probes and
the D10.8 source citation. A row
names the line that implements the rule and the
text that breaks it. The stages run from the cheapest to the widest: the
emitted-text suites first, then every unit test, then the product tests.
69 of the 72 were caught by the first stage.
The second stage excludes mutate_selftest, which reads this table against the
live sources: a round mutates one of them, so the test fails inside the round
and the row reads caught when no test of the compiler saw the mutation
(T-078, round 2, must-fix 1). test/mutate_test.py skips that class on a
mutated tree as well, so a table that forgets the -E is safe too. That skip
is measured over all 88 rows of this table, one at a time, and not over a
sample: three rows repeat their replacement text and the first version of
the guard was dead for them (T-078, round 3, must-fix 1).
build: ninja -C build/debug fort_bootstrap0 gen_test gen_aggregate_test gen_alloc_test gen_call_test gen_cast_test gen_check_test gen_control_test gen_decl_test gen_defer_test gen_enum_test gen_global_test gen_module_test gen_own_test gen_span_test gen_string_test gen_switch_test gen_symbols_test driver_test driver_check_test driver_conformance_test driver_ast_test driver_tokens_test selfcheck_test runtime_sig_test types_abi_test mem_test

stages.name: every unit test
stages.command: ninja -C build/debug && cd build/debug && ctest -L unit -E mutate_selftest -j 6 --output-on-failure
